Test step A2 of the build plan at `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-83+84/plan.md` (search for `### A2 — Add the` for the full spec — read it in full, this prompt summarises but isn't a substitute).

## What was built

`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/index.tsx` (+ its `index.test.tsx` + `index.stories.tsx`) gained a fourth variation, `recentlyViewed` (SFCC-83's rail tile): every existing `VARIATION_CONFIG` flag is `false`, plus a brand-new `showContent` flag (also `false` only for this variation) that suppresses the composed `ZimmProductCardContent` child entirely. Since that child owns the card's only real link (keyboard-reachable, accessible name = product name), a small replacement `Link` (react-router-dom, wrapping `ZimmProductCardMedia` directly) was added in the `!config.showContent` render branch, with the product name as `VisuallyHidden` text supplying the link's accessible name, and `alt: ''` overridden on the copies of `primaryImage`/`hoverImage` passed to `ZimmProductCardMedia` in that branch only (so the image's own alt text doesn't get redundantly concatenated onto the link's accessible name).

Read the current `index.tsx`, `index.test.tsx`, and `index.stories.tsx` in full before testing anything — don't rely solely on this summary.

## Specific things to independently verify, not just re-read

1. **Redo the fail-first proof yourself, don't trust the implementer's self-report.** Temporarily flip `showBadge: true` on the `recentlyViewed` row in `VARIATION_CONFIG`, run only the badge-suppression test, confirm it actually fails, then revert and confirm the suite is green again. Do the same for `showHoverImageSwap: true`. Report the actual failure output you saw, not just "it failed."
2. **The accessible-name fix.** Confirm the rendered link's accessible name is *exactly* the product name (e.g. `screen.getByRole('link', {name: 'Natura Dress'})` with no partial/regex match needed) — not just that a test asserting this currently passes, but that it would genuinely *fail* if the `alt: ''` override were removed (try removing it locally, confirm the test breaks, put it back).
3. **`grep -n 'variation ===\|switch (variation)' index.tsx`** — confirm zero real hits (the one match should only be the docblock's own self-referential mention of this exact grep command in a comment, not real branching logic).
4. **`ZimmProductCardContent` genuinely does not mount for `recentlyViewed`** — confirm `document.querySelector('[data-card-slot="content"]')` is null even when `currentPrice`/`badge`/other Content-relevant props are supplied (proving they're suppressed, not just never passed).
5. **Keyboard reachability, for real** — render a `recentlyViewed` card and Tab to it; confirm it's reachable and that Enter/Space would activate a real `<a href>` (not a div with a JS handler). Check the rendered DOM's actual `href` attribute value, not just that `to={href}` was passed as a prop.
6. **Click behaviour parity with the other three variations** — for `home`/`plp`/`wishlist`, `handleMediaClick` handles Cmd/Ctrl/Shift/middle-click by bailing out (letting the browser handle it natively via the stretched overlay). For `recentlyViewed`, there's no `handleMediaClick` at all — confirm this doesn't need to exist here: a real anchor already handles all of those modifier/button cases natively with zero JS, so there's nothing to test-and-possibly-regress. Note this in your report rather than treating its absence as a gap.
7. **Type-level enforcement** — confirm assigning `colour`/`size`/`onRemove`/`onAddToBag`/`sizeChipValues` (any PLP/Wishlist-only field) to `ZimmProductCardBaseProps & ZimmProductCardRecentlyViewedVariation` genuinely fails to compile (not just that a `@ts-expect-error` comment exists — confirm it's *needed*, i.e. remove it locally and confirm `tsc` now complains about an unused directive would NOT occur — rather confirm removing the directive causes a real compile error to surface).
8. **`hideBagOnMobile`'s inline comment** cites a real Figma node ID (not a placeholder).
9. **Storybook**: the `RecentlyViewed` story should visually show nothing but a single bare image — no visible name, price, badge, or bag. If you can build/check Storybook, confirm this; if not, confirm the story's own args don't pass anything (`hoverImage`, `badge`, `onAddToBag`, etc.) that would misleadingly imply those apply.
10. **Regression check on the other three variations** — confirm `home`/`plp`/`wishlist` are byte-identical in rendered behaviour to before this change (the `showContent: true` addition to their config rows should be a pure no-op for them). Spot-check by running the existing (pre-A2) test suites for those three and confirming nothing broke — the full `npm run test` run should already show this, but call out specifically if anything in the `home`/`plp`/`wishlist` describe blocks needed any change at all to keep passing (it shouldn't have).

## Gates to run and report real output for

`npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run test`, `npm run lint` (compare against baseline: 26 problems / 5 errors / 21 warnings — report the delta, not just whether it exits 0), `node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` (baseline: 2 unacknowledged, both pre-existing in unrelated files — confirm no new ones).

## What NOT to do

Do not fix anything you find — report it. Do not modify any file (you may make temporary local edits to prove a fail-first case as instructed above, but revert every one of them before finishing, and confirm via `git diff`/`git status` that the working tree matches exactly what it was before you started, modulo nothing).

Report findings labelled CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE and UNIFORM/ONE-OFF where relevant, what you tried to falsify and couldn't, and anything you could not verify (say so explicitly rather than staying silent).

1	# SFCC-83 + SFCC-84 — Build Plan
2	
3	**Produced:** 2026-09-06 · **Gate:** `findings.md` (four passes, cleared at the 2026-09-06 adjudication)
4	**Base branch:** `feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component` (PR #85, open, unmerged)
5	
6	## 1. Goal statement
7	
8	Build the Recently Viewed rail and its full-history page per **SFCC-83** and **SFCC-84** (ACs in Jira
9	`customfield_10231`), designed in **`Zimmermann_Design_System_2026` component set `40000587:38471`**
10	(Desktop `40000307:12444`, Tablet `40000730:13363`, Mobile `40000538:25030` — all authoritative,
11	corroborated by PDP-template instances `7998:13508` / `8272:28947`), with SFCC-84's page from the
12	**provisional** `Zimmermann_Designs` `3332:35655` — following `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`
13	(token hierarchy) and `.claude/rules/components.md` (container/presentational split), and extending
14	**PR #85 / SFCC-236's** `ZimmProductCard` family via a **new `VARIATION_CONFIG` entry** (not a new
15	card), a **copy-first override of `recommended-products/`**, and **co-located `<name>.css.ts`**
16	recipes registered in `theme/components/index.ts`.
17	
18	Scope follows `.docs/prd/search.md` §7.4 (PDP + Cart). **PLP is out**; SFCC-83 AC 9 knowingly not met.
19	**No consent gating** (development-phase carve-out, Marcel 2026-09-06) — must be stated in both PR
20	bodies; must not reach production.
21	
22	## 2. Scale call
23	
24	### Architecture fork — resolved: override `recommended-products/`, which removes the Cart port
25	
26	Verified directly at `node_modules/@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev/configs/webpack/overrides-plugin.js`.
27	`isFromExtends` returns true when the request names `@salesforce/retail-react-app` **and the issuing
28	file is not itself inside `overrides/`**. The plugin's own comment (lines 116–127): *"This will return
29	true if the issuer is a file in a base template... This allow the base template to import from
30	overrides."* Implementation: `this.extends.includes(pkgName) && !filepath.includes(issuerPath)`.
31	
32	Base Cart imports at `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/cart/index.jsx:36`:
33	`import RecommendedProducts from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/recommended-products'`
34	— a package-path import issued from a base file, so it **is** redirected once our override exists.
35	Base Cart is itself loaded by base `routes.jsx` via a relative `import('./pages/cart')`, which is not
36	redirected — so base Cart keeps rendering and picks up our override for free.
37	
38	**Consequence: the ~2,460-line Cart copy-first (`index.jsx` 1515 + 8 real partials ≈ 948) is not
39	required.** This departed from adjudication item #10 ("we only have to copy-first for cart"), in the
40	direction of *less* work. **APPROVED by Marcel, 2026-09-06**, on the evidence that this is already the
41	dominant pattern in this repo: nine component overrides shadow base paths and are reached purely by
42	the resolver (`icons` at 64 base import sites — and mandated by AGENTS.md — `responsive` 12,
43	`product-view` 6, `drawer-menu`/`list-menu` 2 each, `header`/`footer` 1 each). The single page port
44	(`product-detail`) exists only because base `routes.jsx` loads pages by *relative* import, which the
45	resolver never redirects — a constraint that does not apply to components. Open Question 5 is closed.
46	
47	**Caveat:** this is a *build-time webpack* resolver. It runs in the dev server and production build
48	only — **not** Storybook (`.storybook/main.js` aliases straight to `node_modules`) and **not** Vitest.
49	So the Cart behaviour cannot be proven by any automated test in this repo; it must be checked in the
50	running app. That is why A1's pause is a hard gate.
51	
52	Cost of this choice: the override module loads at **four base import sites serving eight rails**, not
53	five as an earlier draft of this plan stated:
54	
55	| Base import site | Rails | Takes the new branch? |
56	|---|---|---|
57	| `app/pages/cart/index.jsx:36` | Cart Recently Viewed, Cart May-Also-Like | **Yes** (1 of 2) |
58	| `app/pages/product-detail/index.jsx:40` | *(shadowed by our own PDP override — 3 rails)* | **Yes** (1 of 3) |
59	| `app/hooks/use-add-to-cart-modal.js:30` | add-to-cart modal (`pdp-similar-items`) | No |
60	| `app/pages/product-list/partials/empty-results.jsx:20` | PLP empty-search top-sellers, most-viewed | No |
61	
62	It is therefore a **faithful port plus exactly one branch**, keyed off
63	`EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED` (`'viewed-recently-einstein'` — the same string as
64	`CART_RECENTLY_VIEWED`, `constants.js:156,160`). **Two rails take the new branch; the other six must
65	render identically before and after** — a hard pass criterion.
66	
67	**🔴 Correction, 2026-09-06 — the PDP row above is misleading, verified directly against
68	`overrides-plugin.js`'s actual source, not just this plan's earlier paraphrase of it.** The
69	table's "Yes (1 of 3)" for `product-detail/index.jsx:40` describes the **base** file's import —
70	but that file is shadowed by our own PDP override page and never loads. What actually matters is
71	*our own* `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx`'s import of `RecommendedProducts`, and
72	`isFromExtends` (`overrides-plugin.js:128-146`) returns **false** whenever the issuing file is
73	itself inside `overrides/` — its own doc comment says so plainly: *"This will return false if the
74	issuer is a file in the overrides dir."* Our PDP page's current package-path import
75	(`product-detail/index.tsx:59`) is therefore **not** redirected to our override, at all, regardless
76	of `Island`, scroll position, or Einstein data — none of which were ever the actual blocker.
77	Discovered live during A1's mandatory Cart/PDP verification (Marcel: zero marker fires on PDP even
78	after a full scroll to the bottom, while Cart fired correctly and repeatedly).
79	
80	**Consequence, and why this isn't just a testing nuisance:** as originally planned, PDP's Recently
81	Viewed rail would never render even after A6 lands the branch — Cart would work, PDP would
82	silently not, and SFCC-83's PDP requirement would ship broken with no test catching it (no PR-time
83	E2E on this path either, per the Loop depth section below). **Fix, folded into A6 (Marcel,
84	2026-09-06):** change `product-detail/index.tsx:59`'s `RecommendedProducts` import from the base
85	package path to a relative path pointing at our own override, per
86	`.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`'s existing "Importing an already-overridden component from a
87	new component" rule — the exact same doctrine
88	A6 already applies to `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` below, just missed for `RecommendedProducts` itself
89	in the original draft of this plan. See A6's updated step and pass criteria.
90	
91	Two of those six are on **PLP**, explicitly descoped at adjudication #2. The override *loads* there
92	but its branch never fires (those rails use `EMPTY_SEARCH_RESULTS_*` recommenders), so **no Recently
93	Viewed rail appears on PLP**. State this in the PR body so a reviewer does not read the override's
94	presence on PLP as scope creep.
95	
96	Rejected alternative — re-homing the fetch into a new Zimmermann container: still needs a per-surface
97	caller, and Cart is a base page we cannot pass props to without the 2,460-line port. Buys nothing,
98	costs the port.
99	
100	### Branch: ONE, single PR (Marcel, 2026-09-06)
101	
102	**`feature/SFCC-83-84_recently-viewed`**, cut from `feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component`.
103	
104	An earlier draft proposed two stacked branches. **Marcel chose a single branch / single PR to
105	maintain**, which is now the plan. Step IDs keep their `A*`/`B*` prefixes (they read as "rail work"
106	and "page work") but execute as one sequence on one branch:
107	
108	> A1 → A2 → A3 → A4 → A5 → A6 → B1 → B2 → B3 → GATES
109	
110	**What this buys:**
111	- **The AC 5 / AC 84-1 split disappears.** Those two ACs are the *same* requirement. On two branches
112	  the rail would have shipped with an unsupplied `seeAllHref` and SFCC-83 could not be marked Done
113	  until the second PR merged. On one branch the link and its destination land together — no
114	  interim state where the link points at a 404, and both stories close on one merge.
115	- One review conversation, one CI run, one changelog entry.
116	
117	**What it costs, stated plainly:**
118	- **The four-team CODEOWNERS fan-out on `overrides/app/routes.tsx` (`CODEOWNERS:94`) now applies to
119	  the whole PR**, not just the page half. Every reviewer group sees the full diff.
120	- **The provisional-design page now gates the confirmed-design rail.** SFCC-83's rail is authoritative
121	  at all three viewports and corroborated twice; SFCC-84's page comes entirely from a provisional
122	  source. If the page's design is challenged in review, the rail — which re-skins two live surfaces
123	  and has no such doubt — waits with it. Accepted deliberately; flag it in the PR body so a reviewer
124	  knows the rail can be split back out if the page stalls.
125	
126	### Loop depth
127	
128	Two stories, ~22 files, one 236-line copy-first file. Mid-size build.
129	
130	- **Full implementer → tester → scorer** on A2, A3, A4, A5, B1, B3 — where a silent wrong answer
131	  ships (a variation flag misread from Figma; an ordering/cap bug of exactly the shape the FED
132	  handbook's finding 18 warns encodes itself into a passing test; an AC-8 gate that never fires).
133	- **Implementer + scorer only** on A1, A6, B2, A7, B4 — their gate is mechanical (`tsc`, `npm run
134	  test`, a diff read); a tester pass adds a round-trip without adding a check.
135	
136	**Deliberately dropped, with reasons:**
137	- **No Playwright/E2E.** Adding an allow-list group to `.github/workflows/qa.yml` is Tier 1 CI config
138	  (`CODEOWNERS:65`) — out of scope. Without it these paths resolve to `e2e_scope: skip` and there is
139	  no PR-time E2E run either way (`.claude/rules/testing.md` > Change-scoped E2E). State this in both
140	  PR bodies rather than implying coverage exists.
141	- **No page-level Storybook story.** No page in this repo has one; the presentational organisms carry
142	  the stories, matching `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/partials/*.stories.tsx`.
143	- **No new `theme/components/*Shared.ts`.** Both recipes derive media queries from `breakpoints`
144	  imported from `app/theme/foundation` — one source, two importers, no copied literal.
145	- **No visual-regression tooling.** None exists; Figma parity is checked by eye against named nodes.
146	
147	## 3. File manifest
148	
149	Tiers from `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md`, `.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md`, `CODEOWNERS` — **never**
150	`.claude/registry/*.md`. **No Tier 1 file is touched. Nothing is BLOCKED.**
151	
152	### Rail work (SFCC-83)
153	
154	| File | Action | Tier | Owner |
155	|---|---|---|---|
156	| `overrides/app/components/recommended-products/index.tsx` | CREATE (copy-first, 236 lines) | **Tier 2** | `pwa-squad-b` + `tier-2-approvers` + `tier-1-approvers` (`CODEOWNERS:104`) |
157	| `overrides/app/components/recommended-products/index.test.tsx` | CREATE | **Tier 2** | as above |
158	| `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/index.tsx` | MODIFY (union member + `VARIATION_CONFIG` row + docblock) | Tier 3 | `pwa-squad-a` + `pwa-squad-b` (`CODEOWNERS:176`) |
159	| `.../zimmProductCard/index.test.tsx` | MODIFY | Tier 3 | as above |
160	| `.../zimmProductCard/index.stories.tsx` | MODIFY | Tier 3 | as above |
161	| `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmRecentlyViewedRail/index.tsx` | CREATE | Tier 3 | `pwa-squad-a` + `pwa-squad-b` |
162	| `.../zimmRecentlyViewedRail/zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts` | CREATE | Tier 3 | squads only (`CODEOWNERS:186`, last-match-wins) |
163	| `.../zimmRecentlyViewedRail/index.stories.tsx` | CREATE | Tier 3 | as above |
164	| `.../zimmRecentlyViewedRail/index.test.tsx` | CREATE | Tier 3 | as above |
165	| `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` | MODIFY (register `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail`) | **Tier 2** | `tier-2-approvers` + `tier-1-approvers` (`CODEOWNERS:117`) |
166	| `overrides/app/utils/recentlyViewedCard.ts` | CREATE | Untiered | — |
167	| `overrides/app/utils/recentlyViewedCard.test.ts` | CREATE | Untiered | — |
168	| `overrides/app/hooks/useRecentlyViewedGate.ts` | CREATE | Untiered — **not** on either protected hook list; no CODEOWNERS glob covers `overrides/app/hooks/*` generically | — |
169	| `overrides/app/hooks/useRecentlyViewedGate.test.ts` | CREATE | Untiered | — |

173	**Explicitly not modified:** `zimmProductCard/zimmProductCard.css.ts`. The new variation sets only
174	`showBadge` / `showHoverImageSwap`, both consumed in `index.tsx`, never in the recipe. If a change
175	there appears necessary, **stop** — it means the variation was modelled wrongly.
176	
177	### Page work (SFCC-84)
178	
179	| File | Action | Tier | Owner |
180	|---|---|---|---|
181	| `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmRecentlyViewedGrid/index.tsx` | CREATE | Tier 3 | `pwa-squad-a` + `pwa-squad-b` |
182	| `.../zimmRecentlyViewedGrid/zimmRecentlyViewedGrid.css.ts` | CREATE | Tier 3 | as above (`CODEOWNERS:186`) |
183	| `.../zimmRecentlyViewedGrid/index.stories.tsx` | CREATE | Tier 3 | as above |
184	| `.../zimmRecentlyViewedGrid/index.test.tsx` | CREATE | Tier 3 | as above |
185	| `overrides/app/pages/recentlyViewed/index.tsx` | CREATE (container) | Untiered — no CODEOWNERS rule | — |
186	| `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` | MODIFY (register `ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid`) | **Tier 2** | `tier-2-approvers` + `tier-1-approvers` |
187	| `overrides/app/routes.tsx` | MODIFY (one route entry) | **Tier 2 Global Shell** | 4 teams (`CODEOWNERS:94`) — highest fan-out in this work |

190	
191	**Two protection tiers are touched** (Tier 2 + Tier 3). AGENTS.md Hard Rule #10 requires confirming
192	scope with the developer — one confirmation at plan approval covers the single PR.
193	
194	## 4. Steps
195	
196	One commit per step. `conventions.md`'s no-magic-strings rule throughout: `'viewed-recently-einstein'`
197	is only ever referenced as `EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED`.
198	
199	### A1 — Copy-first: `recommended-products` override *(AGENTS.md step 3 — mandatory pause)*
200	
201	Copy `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/recommended-products/index.jsx`
202	verbatim to `overrides/app/components/recommended-products/index.tsx`; convert to TypeScript (replace
203	`PropTypes` with a `type`, type all params/returns, no `any`/`@ts-ignore`); add
204	`console.log('[overrides] recommended-products/index.tsx')`. **No functional change whatsoever.**
205	Then **STOP and present to Marcel** to verify the override renders on both PDP and Cart.
206	
207	**Pass criteria**
208	- `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0.
209	- Diff vs base is TypeScript-only: no changed JSX, hook calls, prop names, or reordered `useEffect`s.
210	- `propTypes` removed, replaced by a `RecommendedProductsProps` type; the `...props` passthrough to
211	  `ProductScroller` preserved.
212	- `ProductScroller` and `use-einstein` imports stay on `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` base paths —
213	  no local override exists for either, so `overrideStyling.md`'s relative-import rule does not apply.
214	- Marcel confirms the marker log fires on a **Cart** visit. **This is the direct proof the resolver
215	  reaches base pages and no Cart port is needed** — and the only possible proof, since Storybook/
216	  Vitest do not load the resolver. Confirmed 2026-09-06.
217	- **PDP is correctly expected to show zero fires at this step — do not treat that as a failure.**
218	  `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` is itself an overrides file, so its package-path
219	  import of `RecommendedProducts` is never redirected by the resolver (`isFromExtends` returns
220	  `false` for an issuer inside `overrides/` — see the correction in §2 "Architecture fork"). PDP
221	  only becomes reachable once A6 changes that file's import to relative — verified there instead,
222	  by sight, not by this marker (A6 removes the marker).
223	- Commit does **not** remove the `console.log` — that happens in A6.
224	
225	### A2 — Add the `recentlyViewed` variation to `ZimmProductCard`
226	
227	Add `ZimmProductCardRecentlyViewedVariation` to the exported union and one `VARIATION_CONFIG` row.
228	Update the docblock's KNOWN GAP paragraph (lines 124–135) from "whoever builds SFCC-83 needs to…" to a

# SFCC-83 + SFCC-84 — Build Plan

**Produced:** 2026-09-06 · **Gate:** `findings.md` (four passes, cleared at the 2026-09-06 adjudication)
**Base branch:** `feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component` (PR #85, open, unmerged)

## 1. Goal statement

Build the Recently Viewed rail and its full-history page per **SFCC-83** and **SFCC-84** (ACs in Jira
`customfield_10231`), designed in **`Zimmermann_Design_System_2026` component set `40000587:38471`**
(Desktop `40000307:12444`, Tablet `40000730:13363`, Mobile `40000538:25030` — all authoritative,
corroborated by PDP-template instances `7998:13508` / `8272:28947`), with SFCC-84's page from the
**provisional** `Zimmermann_Designs` `3332:35655` — following `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`
(token hierarchy) and `.claude/rules/components.md` (container/presentational split), and extending
**PR #85 / SFCC-236's** `ZimmProductCard` family via a **new `VARIATION_CONFIG` entry** (not a new
card), a **copy-first override of `recommended-products/`**, and **co-located `<name>.css.ts`**
recipes registered in `theme/components/index.ts`.

Scope follows `.docs/prd/search.md` §7.4 (PDP + Cart). **PLP is out**; SFCC-83 AC 9 knowingly not met.
**No consent gating** (development-phase carve-out, Marcel 2026-09-06) — must be stated in both PR
bodies; must not reach production.

## 2. Scale call

### Architecture fork — resolved: override `recommended-products/`, which removes the Cart port

Verified directly at `node_modules/@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev/configs/webpack/overrides-plugin.js`.
`isFromExtends` returns true when the request names `@salesforce/retail-react-app` **and the issuing
file is not itself inside `overrides/`**. The plugin's own comment (lines 116–127): *"This will return
true if the issuer is a file in a base template... This allow the base template to import from
overrides."* Implementation: `this.extends.includes(pkgName) && !filepath.includes(issuerPath)`.

Base Cart imports at `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/cart/index.jsx:36`:
`import RecommendedProducts from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/recommended-products'`
— a package-path import issued from a base file, so it **is** redirected once our override exists.
Base Cart is itself loaded by base `routes.jsx` via a relative `import('./pages/cart')`, which is not
redirected — so base Cart keeps rendering and picks up our override for free.

**Consequence: the ~2,460-line Cart copy-first (`index.jsx` 1515 + 8 real partials ≈ 948) is not
required.** This departed from adjudication item #10 ("we only have to copy-first for cart"), in the
direction of *less* work. **APPROVED by Marcel, 2026-09-06**, on the evidence that this is already the
dominant pattern in this repo: nine component overrides shadow base paths and are reached purely by
the resolver (`icons` at 64 base import sites — and mandated by AGENTS.md — `responsive` 12,
`product-view` 6, `drawer-menu`/`list-menu` 2 each, `header`/`footer` 1 each). The single page port
(`product-detail`) exists only because base `routes.jsx` loads pages by *relative* import, which the
resolver never redirects — a constraint that does not apply to components. Open Question 5 is closed.

**Caveat:** this is a *build-time webpack* resolver. It runs in the dev server and production build
only — **not** Storybook (`.storybook/main.js` aliases straight to `node_modules`) and **not** Vitest.
So the Cart behaviour cannot be proven by any automated test in this repo; it must be checked in the
running app. That is why A1's pause is a hard gate.

Cost of this choice: the override module loads at **four base import sites serving eight rails**, not
five as an earlier draft of this plan stated:

| Base import site | Rails | Takes the new branch? |
|---|---|---|
| `app/pages/cart/index.jsx:36` | Cart Recently Viewed, Cart May-Also-Like | **Yes** (1 of 2) |
| `app/pages/product-detail/index.jsx:40` | *(shadowed by our own PDP override — 3 rails)* | **Yes** (1 of 3) |
| `app/hooks/use-add-to-cart-modal.js:30` | add-to-cart modal (`pdp-similar-items`) | No |
| `app/pages/product-list/partials/empty-results.jsx:20` | PLP empty-search top-sellers, most-viewed | No |

It is therefore a **faithful port plus exactly one branch**, keyed off
`EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED` (`'viewed-recently-einstein'` — the same string as
`CART_RECENTLY_VIEWED`, `constants.js:156,160`). **Two rails take the new branch; the other six must
render identically before and after** — a hard pass criterion.

**🔴 Correction, 2026-09-06 — the PDP row above is misleading, verified directly against
`overrides-plugin.js`'s actual source, not just this plan's earlier paraphrase of it.** The
table's "Yes (1 of 3)" for `product-detail/index.jsx:40` describes the **base** file's import —
but that file is shadowed by our own PDP override page and never loads. What actually matters is
*our own* `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx`'s import of `RecommendedProducts`, and
`isFromExtends` (`overrides-plugin.js:128-146`) returns **false** whenever the issuing file is
itself inside `overrides/` — its own doc comment says so plainly: *"This will return false if the
issuer is a file in the overrides dir."* Our PDP page's current package-path import
(`product-detail/index.tsx:59`) is therefore **not** redirected to our override, at all, regardless
of `Island`, scroll position, or Einstein data — none of which were ever the actual blocker.
Discovered live during A1's mandatory Cart/PDP verification (Marcel: zero marker fires on PDP even
after a full scroll to the bottom, while Cart fired correctly and repeatedly).

**Consequence, and why this isn't just a testing nuisance:** as originally planned, PDP's Recently
Viewed rail would never render even after A6 lands the branch — Cart would work, PDP would
silently not, and SFCC-83's PDP requirement would ship broken with no test catching it (no PR-time
E2E on this path either, per the Loop depth section below). **Fix, folded into A6 (Marcel,
2026-09-06):** change `product-detail/index.tsx:59`'s `RecommendedProducts` import from the base
package path to a relative path pointing at our own override, per
`.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`'s existing "Importing an already-overridden component from a
new component" rule — the exact same doctrine

### A4 — AC-8 gate hook, plus the PDP write

Create `overrides/app/hooks/useRecentlyViewedGate.ts`.

This answers **finding 28** — the recommender returns a two-product baseline for a visitor with zero
history, so `recs.length === 0` never fires and AC 8 is not implementable from the response. The gate
is a **local boolean**, not a copy of Einstein's list:

```
hasRecentlyViewed = sessionFlagIsSet || isRegistered
```

- `markProductViewed()` writes a session-scoped flag to `sessionStorage`, called from the existing
  Einstein `useEffect` in `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` (lines 772–801), alongside
  the `einstein.sendViewProduct` calls already there. One import, one call, guarded by the same
  `if (product)`.
- `isRegistered` from `useCustomerType()` — the same hook `use-einstein.js:449` already uses.

**Why this maps the ACs exactly:** `sessionStorage` is literally session-scoped and cleared at session
end — **AC 6**. `isRegistered` short-circuits the local flag, so an authenticated shopper on a device
they have never browsed on still gets server-side history — **AC 7**. It is a strict improvement on
trusting Einstein alone: the SLAS `usid` can outlive a browser session, so this gate makes AC 6 *true*
rather than assumed.

**Stated assumption (must appear in the PR body):** a *registered* shopper who has genuinely never
viewed anything still sees the two-product baseline. That residual is owned by Open Question 6. Do not
paper over it with a heuristic.

- SSR-safe: initial state `false`, resolved in `useEffect`. No `sessionStorage` access during render.

- Wrapped in `try/catch` — Safari private mode throws on `sessionStorage`. Failure degrades to `false`

- JSDoc with `@returns` (`components.md` > Hooks).
- Vitest: no flag + guest → `false`; flag + guest → `true`; no flag + registered → `true`;

addedLines: - agent-sdk-dev:agent-sdk-verifier-py: Use this agent to verify that a Python Agent SDK application is properly configured, follows SDK best practices and documentation recommendations, and is ready for deployment or testing. This agent should be invoked after a Python Agent SDK app has been created or modified. (Tools: All tools)

- agent-sdk-dev:agent-sdk-verifier-ts: Use this agent to verify that a TypeScript Agent SDK application is properly configured, follows SDK best practices and documentation recommendations, and is ready for deployment or testing. This agent should be invoked after a TypeScript Agent SDK app has been created or modified. (Tools: All tools)
- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- code-simplifier:code-simplifier: Simplifies and refines code for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. Focuses on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise. (Tools: All tools)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- feature-dev:code-architect: Designs feature architectures by analyzing existing codebase patterns and conventions, then providing comprehensive implementation blueprints with specific files to create/modify, component designs, data flows, and build sequences (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- feature-dev:code-explorer: Deeply analyzes existing codebase features by tracing execution paths, mapping architecture layers, understanding patterns and abstractions, and documenting dependencies to inform new development (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- feature-dev:code-reviewer: Reviews code for bugs, logic errors, security vulnerabilities, code quality issues, and adherence to project conventions, using confidence-based filtering to report only high-priority issues that truly matter (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- plugin-dev:agent-creator: Use this agent when the user asks to "create an agent", "generate an agent", "build a new agent", "make me an agent that...", or describes agent functionality they need. Trigger when user wants to create autonomous agents for plugins. Examples:

<example>
Context: User wants to create a code review agent
user: "Create an agent that reviews code for quality issues"
assistant: "I'll use the agent-creator agent to generate the agent configuration."
<commentary>
User requesting new agent creation, trigger agent-creator to generate it.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: User describes needed functionality
user: "I need an agent that generates unit tests for my code"
assistant: "I'll use the agent-creator agent to create a test generation agent."
<commentary>
User describes agent need, trigger agent-creator to build it.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: User wants to add agent to plugin
user: "Add an agent to my plugin that validates configurations"
assistant: "I'll use the agent-creator agent to generate a configuration validator agent."
<commentary>
Plugin development with agent addition, trigger agent-creator.
</commentary>
</example> (Tools: Write, Read)

- plugin-dev:plugin-validator: Use this agent when the user asks to "validate my plugin", "check plugin structure", "verify plugin is correct", "validate plugin.json", "check plugin files", or mentions plugin validation. Also trigger proactively after user creates or modifies plugin components. Examples:

<example>
Context: User finished creating a new plugin
user: "I've created my first plugin with commands and hooks"
assistant: "Great! Let me validate the plugin structure."
<commentary>
Plugin created, proactively validate to catch issues early.
</commentary>
assistant: "I'll use the plugin-validator agent to check the plugin."
</example>

<example>
Context: User explicitly requests validation
user: "Validate my plugin before I publish it"
assistant: "I'll use the plugin-validator agent to perform comprehensive validation."
<commentary>
Explicit validation request triggers the agent.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: User modified plugin.json
user: "I've updated the plugin manifest"
assistant: "Let me validate the changes."
<commentary>
Manifest modified, validate to ensure correctness.
</commentary>
assistant: "I'll use the plugin-validator agent to check the manifest."
</example> (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- plugin-dev:skill-reviewer: Use this agent when the user has created or modified a skill and needs quality review, asks to "review my skill", "check skill quality", "improve skill description", or wants to ensure skill follows best practices. Trigger proactively after skill creation. Examples:

<example>
Context: User just created a new skill
user: "I've created a PDF processing skill"
assistant: "Great! Let me review the skill quality."
<commentary>
Skill created, proactively trigger skill-reviewer to ensure it follows best practices.
</commentary>
assistant: "I'll use the skill-reviewer agent to review the skill."
</example>

<example>
Context: User requests skill review
user: "Review my skill and tell me how to improve it"
assistant: "I'll use the skill-reviewer agent to analyze the skill quality."
<commentary>
Explicit skill review request triggers the agent.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: User modified skill description
user: "I updated the skill description, does it look good?"
assistant: "I'll use the skill-reviewer agent to review the changes."
<commentary>
Skill description modified, review for triggering effectiveness.
</commentary>
</example> (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob)

- pr-review-toolkit:code-reviewer: Use this agent when you need to review code for adherence to project guidelines, style guides, and best practices. This agent should be used proactively after writing or modifying code, especially before committing changes or creating pull requests. It will check for style violations, potential issues, and ensure code follows the established patterns in CLAUDE.md. Also the agent needs to know which files to focus on for the review. In most cases this will be recently completed work which is unstaged in git (can be retrieved by running git diff). However there can be cases where this is different, make sure to specify this as the agent input when calling the agent. Typical triggers include the user asking for a review of a feature they just implemented, the assistant proactively reviewing its own newly-written code before declaring a task done, and a final pre-PR check before opening a pull request. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:code-simplifier: Use this agent when code has been written or modified and needs to be simplified for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. This agent should be triggered automatically after completing a coding task or writing a logical chunk of code. It simplifies code by following project best practices while retaining all functionality. The agent focuses only on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise.

Examples:

<example>
Context: The assistant has just implemented a new feature that adds user authentication to an API endpoint.
user: "Please add authentication to the /api/users endpoint"
assistant: "I've implemented the authentication for the /api/users endpoint. Here's the code:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
Since a logical chunk of code has been written (authentication feature), use the Task tool to launch the code-simplifier agent to improve the code's clarity and maintainability while preserving functionality.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now let me use the code-simplifier agent to refine this implementation for better clarity and maintainability"
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just fixed a bug by adding several conditional checks.
user: "Fix the null pointer exception in the data processor"
assistant: "I've added the necessary null checks to prevent the exception:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After modifying code to fix a bug, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the fix follows best practices and maintains code quality.
</commentary>
assistant: "Let me refine this bug fix using the code-simplifier agent to ensure it follows our best practices"
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just refactored a function to improve performance.
user: "Optimize the data sorting algorithm for better performance"
assistant: "I've optimized the sorting algorithm. Here's the updated implementation:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After completing a performance optimization task, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and maintainable.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now I'll use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and follows our coding standards"
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:comment-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to analyze code comments for accuracy, completeness, and long-term maintainability. This includes (1) after generating large documentation comments or docstrings, (2) before finalizing a pull request that adds or modifies comments, (3) when reviewing existing comments for potential technical debt or comment rot, and (4) when you need to verify that comments accurately reflect the code they describe. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:pr-test-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to review a pull request for test coverage quality and completeness. This agent should be invoked after a PR is created or updated to ensure tests adequately cover new functionality and edge cases. Typical triggers include the user asking whether tests on a freshly-created PR are thorough, an updated PR adding new logic that needs coverage analysis, and a final pre-merge double-check before marking a PR ready. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:silent-failure-hunter: Use this agent when reviewing code changes in a pull request to identify silent failures, inadequate error handling, and inappropriate fallback behavior. This agent should be invoked proactively after completing a logical chunk of work that involves error handling, catch blocks, fallback logic, or any code that could potentially suppress errors. Examples:

<example>
Context: Daisy has just finished implementing a new feature that fetches data from an API with fallback behavior.
Daisy: "I've added error handling to the API client. Can you review it?"
Assistant: "Let me use the silent-failure-hunter agent to thoroughly examine the error handling in your changes."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example>

<example>
Context: Daisy has created a PR with changes that include try-catch blocks.
Daisy: "Please review PR #1234"
Assistant: "I'll use the silent-failure-hunter agent to check for any silent failures or inadequate error handling in this PR."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example>

<example>
Context: Daisy has just refactored error handling code.
Daisy: "I've updated the error handling in the authentication module"
Assistant: "Let me proactively use the silent-failure-hunter agent to ensure the error handling changes don't introduce silent failures."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:type-design-analyzer: Use this agent when you need expert analysis of type design in your codebase. Specifically use it (1) when introducing a new type to ensure it follows best practices for encapsulation and invariant expression, (2) during pull request creation to review all types being added, and (3) when refactoring existing types to improve their design quality. The agent will provide both qualitative feedback and quantitative ratings on encapsulation, invariant expression, usefulness, and enforcement. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- vercel:ai-architect: Specializes in architecting AI-powered applications on Vercel — choosing between AI SDK patterns, configuring providers, building agents, setting up durable workflows, and integrating MCP servers. Use when designing AI features, building chatbots, or creating agentic applications. (Tools: All tools)

- vercel:deployment-expert: Specializes in Vercel deployment strategies, CI/CD pipelines, preview URLs, production promotions, rollbacks, environment variables, and domain configuration. Use when troubleshooting deployments, setting up CI/CD, or optimizing the deploy pipeline. (Tools: All tools)

- vercel:performance-optimizer: Specializes in optimizing Vercel application performance — Core Web Vitals, rendering strategies, caching, image optimization, font loading, edge computing, and bundle size. Use when investigating slow pages, improving Lighthouse scores, or optimizing loading performance. (Tools: All tools)

- zm-implementer: Executes one step of a Zimmermann PWA Kit build plan. Use when a planned step needs to be implemented in code. Writes only the files the step names, and stops rather than expanding scope. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- zm-orchestrator: Scope and spec-conformance checker for an in-flight Zimmermann build. Use after an implementation step to judge whether the work delivers exactly what the plan specified — neither less nor more. Reports a verdict; never edits code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- zm-planner: Synthesises gathered evidence into an executable build plan for a Zimmermann PWA Kit story. Use after all sources have been gathered, when the findings need to become a sequenced plan with per-step pass criteria. Does not gather evidence itself and does not write code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, WebFetch)

- zm-scorer: Scores an implemented and tested Zimmermann build step and decides PASS or return-to-implementer. Use after the Tester reports. Judges quality against six axes; never edits code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- zm-tester: Tests an implemented Zimmermann build step across multiple angles and reports findings. Use after the Implementer reports a step done. Finds and reports problems; never fixes them. Dispatches its own sub-agents for parallel angles. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Agent)

14	 * `carousel` / `indicator` are stamped by `ZimmProductCardMedia`; `content` / `bag` / `price` /
15	 * `sizeChips` / `notifyMe` by `ZimmProductCardContent`. Do not rename a value here without
16	 * checking both molecules' own docblocks, which document what each slot is for.
17	 */

24	  content: 'content',

33	 * (desktop arrows, the hover-reveal price/size-selector swap, the notify-me reveal) — the
34	 * resolved SFCC-236 decision that arrows and the touch slide-indicator are mutually exclusive by

 * plus this component family's test suites) reads the same value instead of each independently

 * `carousel` / `indicator` are stamped by `ZimmProductCardMedia`; `content` / `bag` / `price` /
 * `sizeChips` / `notifyMe` by `ZimmProductCardContent`. Do not rename a value here without
 * checking both molecules' own docblocks, which document what each slot is for.
 */

  media: 'media',
  badge: 'badge',
  close: 'close',
  carousel: 'carousel',
  indicator: 'indicator',
  content: 'content',
  bag: 'bag',
  price: 'price',
  sizeChips: 'sizeChips',
  notifyMe: 'notifyMe',
} as const;

/**
 * Hover-capable-pointer gate shared by every hover-only affordance across the card family
 * (desktop arrows, the hover-reveal price/size-selector swap, the notify-me reveal) — the
 * resolved SFCC-236 decision that arrows and the touch slide-indicator are mutually exclusive by
 * pointer capability, not viewport width.

export const HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY = '@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)';

 * change: the organism's own PLP bag-icon mobile hide (`zimmProductCard.css.ts`) and
 * `ZimmProductCardContent`'s responsive outer padding (`zimmProductCardContent.css.ts`).

 * derived this independently from the same `breakpoints.md` token, which is exactly the
 * same-value-typed-twice drift risk a shared constant removes.
 */
export const DESKTOP_QUERY = `@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`;

input.prompt:
You are testing one step ("A2") of an in-flight Zimmermann PWA Kit build, branch `feature/SFCC-83-84_recently-viewed`, repo at /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa. You find problems, you never fix them. Do NOT edit/write/delete any file in the repo — read-only only (Read, Grep, Bash for read-only greps/find; you may run `npx vitest run <specific file>` if genuinely needed to observe existing test output, but do not create new test files or modify any existing one).

## Background
Step A2 added a fourth `variation: 'recentlyViewed'` to the `ZimmProductCard` organism at `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/index.tsx`. When this variation is active (`!config.showContent`), instead of rendering the usual `ZimmProductCardMedia` + `ZimmProductCardContent` pair, the component renders:
```
<MediaOnlyCardLink to={href} display="block">
  <VisuallyHidden>{name}</VisuallyHidden>
  <ZimmProductCardMedia primaryImage={{...primaryImage, alt: ''}} hoverImage={...} images={images} swapOnHover={...} showControls badge={resolvedBadge} />
</MediaOnlyCardLink>
```
where `MediaOnlyCardLink = chakra(RouteLink)` (a plain wrap of react-router-dom's `Link` with Chakra style-prop support — NOT Chakra's own themed `<Link>` component). This is a brand new whole-card interactive element (a real `<a>` wrapping an entire image) that did not exist before this step. The recipe file `zimmProductCard.css.ts` was deliberately NOT touched by this step (confirmed separately) — the plan's own reasoning is that this variation renders no `Card-content` block per Figma (Desktop node `40000307:12444`, Tablet `40000730:13363`, Mobile `40000538:25030`), so none of the recipe's existing hover-reveal machinery (built for the OTHER three variations' stretched-link-overlay pattern) is needed here.

## What I've already independently confirmed myself (do not re-verify these — they are settled, real, CONFIRMED findings, not claims to re-derive)
- Flipping `showBadge`/`showHoverImageSwap` to `true` for this variation makes the corresponding suppression tests fail for real (ran it).
- Removing the `alt: ''` override makes the exact-accessible-name test fail for real, with the actual jsdom-computed accessible name shown as "Natura Dress Zimmermann dress, front" (concatenated) instead of "Natura Dress" (ran it).
- A single Tab reaches the real `<a href="/product/1">` and the next Tab skips past the whole card (ran it) — exactly one focusable element inside this variation's card.
- react-router-dom v5.3.4's real installed `Link` (`node_modules/react-router-dom/cjs/react-router-dom.js`) natively bails out on modifier-clicks/non-primary-button clicks before calling `history.push` — confirmed by reading the actual shipped source, so no click-passthrough handler is needed for this variation.
- **A real, confirmed defect I already found (do not spend time re-finding it, just note it if relevant to your own findings, but your OWN job is the items below):** if a caller supplies MORE than one image to a `recentlyViewed` card (which is type-permitted — `images` is a base prop, not gated per variation — even though the plan says the one real caller, SFCC-83's rail, will always supply exactly one), `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s carousel prev/next `<button>` elements end up nested INSIDE the new `<a>` (confirmed: `link.contains(nextButton) === true`), and clicking a "Next image" button ALSO fires the ancestor anchor's navigation (confirmed: a `<Route path="/product/1">` marker mounted after the click) — a real double-fire bug and invalid nested-interactive-HTML, currently unreachable only because the one specified caller (not yet built) is planned to always pass a single image.

## Your job — investigate these, independently, and report real findings

1. **Focus-ring reset check (the main thing I need from you).** `MediaOnlyCardLink` is a bare `chakra(RouteLink)` — it does NOT get Chakra's own `Link` theme recipe (that only applies if you use Chakra's actual `<Link>` component). It gets no custom `_focus`/`_focusVisible` styling of its own, and the recipe file wasn't touched. So this new whole-card anchor relies entirely on the BROWSER'S default focus outline for a real `<a>`. Search the codebase for anything that resets/removes default focus outlines globally or for anchors specifically — check `overrides/app/theme/globalStyles.ts`, `overrides/app/theme/index.ts`, `overrides/app/theme/foundation/*`, any CSS reset, and Chakra's own default global styles (`theme.styles.global`) for anything like `outline: none`, `outline: 0`, a CSS reset library, or a `*:focus` rule. Also check whether this project's OTHER real anchors (e.g. the stretched-link overlay `<a>` inside `ZimmProductCardContent`'s `ProductNameLink`, or the footer's links) rely on an explicit `:focus-visible` recipe rule rather than the browser default — if EVERY other real link in this component family gets an explicit focus-ring token (`var(--zimm-focus-ring)` etc.) and this is the only one that doesn't, that's a real, concrete, reportable gap (a keyboard user tabbing to this new card-wide link might get no visible focus indicator at all, or an inconsistent one vs. every other card variation) — WCAG 2.4.7. Report exactly what you find, with file:line, and state plainly whether you found evidence of an actual missing focus indicator vs. just an absence of an EXPLICIT one (the implicit browser default might be entirely adequate — say which one it is, don't assume the worse case).
2. **Recipe state exhaustiveness for this new interactive element** (per the standing angle: "for every new interactive part in a recipe, cross-reference the Figma nodes named in the step against the pseudo-states defined in the recipe — `_hover`, `_focusVisible`, `_active`, `_disabled`. A designed state with no recipe entry is a real finding."). Does Figma (per the plan document's own citations — you don't have Figma access, so work from what `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-83+84/plan.md` says, search for "A2 —" and "recentlyViewed") describe ANY hover/focus/active visual treatment for this specific rail-tile card, distinct from the default state? Or does the plan's own evidence suggest the design has no distinct state here at all (in which case this angle is vacuous for this element, and you should say so plainly rather than invent a finding)?
3. **Hover-gating correctness** — is `MediaOnlyCardLink` itself a hover-gated reveal (a hidden-by-default part shown only on hover/focus)? Read the actual render code again: it isn't — it's a plain, always-visible link with no hidden state. Confirm this and state explicitly that this half of the angle is vacuous here (don't force a finding where there is a real absence of the pattern) — UNLESS you find something I've missed (e.g., does `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own carousel-arrow hover-reveal CSS from the shared recipe still apply to the arrows even inside this new branch, in a way that could interact badly with the new Link — you don't need to redo the double-fire proof, just note if the hover-reveal styling itself is a separate concern from the click bug).
4. **Cross-check the AC-4 accessibility narrative against SFCC-236's shared component's OWN test file precedent** — read `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardContent/index.tsx`'s own `ProductNameLink`/link implementation (grep for how IT achieves its accessible name and any focus styling it relies on) and compare: does `ProductNameLink` get an explicit focus style from `zimmProductCard.css.ts` or `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts`, or does IT ALSO rely on the browser default? This tells us whether the new `MediaOnlyCardLink`'s reliance on the default (if that's what you find in #1) is a NEW gap this step introduced, or a pre-existing pattern this step is simply consistent with (in which case it's UNIFORM, not a defect unique to this step).

## Report format
Number your findings to match the 4 items above. Each: file:line, what you found, CONFIRMED (you read/ran something real) or PLAUSIBLE (reasoned), severity (🔴/🟡/🔵), UNIFORM or ONE-OFF. If an item turns out vacuous/clean, say so in one line, don't pad. End with what you could not verify (e.g., you have no way to render this in a real browser to see the ACTUAL visual focus ring — say so).

 * file's own module-private copy, so the two can't silently drift. Governs the price <->
 * size-selector swap below, so both composed children's hover treatments engage together off the

 * `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts`'s own `root` padding step both need the identical `min-width`
 * gate, and a module-private copy in each file was exactly the drift risk this extraction removes.

type ZimmProductCardStyleProps = {
  /** Home only — see VARIATION_CONFIG in index.tsx. Price is hidden at every breakpoint/pointer
   *  type by default and only appears once a hover-capable pointer actually hovers the card. */
  hoverRevealsPrice?: boolean;
  /** PLP + Wishlist — price is visible by default (Content's own natural rendering; no override
   *  needed for that half) and hides only once a hover-capable pointer hovers the card. */
  hoverHidesPrice?: boolean;
  /** PLP + Wishlist — the size-chip picker is hidden at every breakpoint/pointer type by default
   *  and only appears once a hover-capable pointer actually hovers the card, in the same
   *  media-query gate as the price swap above so both engage together. */
  hoverRevealsSizeSelector?: boolean;
  /** Fix C — true whenever ZimmProductCardContent actually mounted a notify-me button
   *  (`isUnavailable && onNotifyMe`, computed once in index.tsx as `showNotifyMe`). Unlike the two
   *  flags above, the "hidden by default" half lives INSIDE `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY`, not outside it
   *  — see docblock point 4: a touch pointer must see notify-me unconditionally (confirmed via
   *  every Mobile Unavailable Figma reference), where price/the size-selector do the opposite. */
  hoverRevealsNotifyMe?: boolean;
  /** Fix C — true for a PLP/Wishlist card that would normally hover-swap to the size-selector
   *  (`config.hoverRevealsSizeSelector`) but is out of stock. Unlike every other flag here, this
   *  is not a pointer-type concern at all: the size-chip wrapper stays hidden permanently, in
   *  every state, on every device — see docblock point 4. */
  sizeSelectorUnavailable?: boolean;
  /** Fix D — PLP only (`VARIATION_CONFIG.plp.hideBagOnMobile` in index.tsx). A viewport-width
   *  concern, not a pointer-type one: hidden below `breakpoints.md`, visible from it up — see
   *  docblock point 5. */
  hideBagOnMobile?: boolean;
};

/**
 * Recipe for the product-card organism (ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard) — composes
 * ZimmProductCardMedia (Step 4) and ZimmProductCardContent (Step 5) with no styling of its own
 * for either child. This recipe's entire job is the cross-component concerns neither child can
 * own by itself:
 *
 *   1. THE STRETCHED-LINK OVERLAY. ZimmProductCardContent's `nameLink` renders the one real `<a>`
 *      in the whole composed tree. Its `::after` is stretched to `inset: 0` against THIS
 *      component's own `root` — the nearest positioned ancestor. Confirmed by reading
 *      `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts` directly: neither its `root` nor `nameRow`, `nameLink`, or
 *      any other part sets `position` anywhere in that file, so nothing between the `<a>` and
 *      this `root` intercepts the containing-block chain. (`ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own `root`
 *      IS `position: relative`, but Media is a *sibling* of Content under this organism's root,
 *      never an ancestor of Content's `<a>`, so it has no bearing on this chain.)
 *   2. LIFTING EVERY OTHER INTERACTIVE CONTROL above that overlay — a z-index higher than the
 *      overlay's own (left unset), or the invisible overlay would intercept their clicks first.
 *      Four separate, single-selector keys rather than one comma-joined selector: verified via
 *      this project's own installed Stylis (v4.2.0 — the same engine Emotion/Chakra invoke at
 *      runtime, confirmed by direct compilation) that a comma-separated list DOES distribute this
 *      recipe's generated class across every branch correctly, but four plain keys need no such
 *      verification to trust at a glance and are each individually addressable from a test. Only
 *      ONE of the four (`content` buttons) also adds `position: relative` — that element is
 *      `position: static` by default in its own component recipe, so a positioned ancestor is
 *      needed for z-index to apply at all. `close`, `carousel`, and `media` are the three
 *      exceptions: `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own recipe already positions each of them directly
 *      (`close` via `position: absolute, top: 0, right: 0`; `carousel` via `position: absolute,
 *      top: 50%, ...`; `media` — its own root — via `position: relative`), so each needs (and
 *      gets) only the z-index bump here:
 *        - `close` — a competing `position` value previously declared alongside it had HIGHER
 *          specificity than Media's own rule (this rule is a class+attribute descendant selector;
 *          Media's is a single class) and silently won the cascade, knocking the remove button out
 *          of its pinned top-right corner into normal document flow (Fix 1). See the inline
 *          comment at that key below and index.test.tsx's "Fix 1" describe block for the proof.

The only new style prop is `` — `display` is a CSS layout keyword, not a design-token-scale prop, so this isn't a semantic-token question at all. Styling conformance - **Recipe state exhaustiveness — vacuous, confirmed clean.** Per `plan.md`'s own citations, `recentlyViewed`'s three Figma nodes (Desktop `40000307:12444`, Tablet `40000730:13363`, Mobile `40000538:25030`) are static per-viewport "everything hidden" instances with no cited Hover/Active/Disabled variant — unlike `home`/`plp`/`wishlist`, which each cite an explicit Default+Hover pair. Confirmed directly by me and independently by a sub-agent. - 🟡 **should-fix, CONFIRMED, ONE-OFF (but see below) — `MediaOnlyCardLink` gets no explicit focus-ring styling, unlike every other interactive control in this component family.** `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/index.tsx:611` (``) has no `_focusVisible`/`outline`/`sx`. I confirmed directly: `grep -n "outline\|_focusVisible" zimmProductCard.css.ts index.tsx` returns nothing touching this element. By contrast, `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts:119-126`'s `nameLink` part (the `ProductNameLink = chakra(RouteLink)` this new code's own comment says it copies — `index.tsx:10-14`) carries an explicit `_focusVisible: { outline: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring)', outlineOffset: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)' }` — I verified this directly too. A sub-agent traced further: Chakra's own `Link` recipe (which would supply an outline reset + focus ring) never applies here because `chakra(RouteLink)` bypasses `useStyleConfig`; no global reset strips the browser default either (the `focus-visible` polyfill correctly excludes real keyboard-Tab focus from the one scoped `outline: none` rule in `globalStyles.ts`, which only targets `.zimm-form-control` anyway) — so **WCAG 2.4.7 is technically satisfied by the browser's native default outline**, but this is a real, visible inconsistency with this design system's own established convention (every other control — `zimmColourSwatch`, `zimmNavItem`, `zimmSizeChip`, `zimmButton`, Media's own `close`/`arrowButton`, Content's `nameLink`/`bagButton`/`notifyMeButton` — carries an explicit `var(--zimm-focus-ring)`-family rule), and it directly contradicts this new code's own doc-comment claim of copying `ProductNameLink`'s pattern (it copied the wrap, not the focus styling). `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts` even states twice, verbatim, that a control sitting on a photo needs the "same uniform ring every other interactive control ... uses" — this is a photo-covering whole-card link with none.
